Lord Ii’s letter in 1847 expresses anxiety that foreign powers have advanced technologically with steamships and modern armies, while Japan risks calamity by sticking to “antiquated systems.” This concern about Western military and technological superiority putting Japan at risk aligns with the events leading to the end of Japan’s isolation.  

Commodore Perry’s expedition in 1853–54 forced Japan to open its ports, demonstrating the exact foreign pressure and technological gap that Lord Ii feared.
